title: AI-Driven Spatio-Temporal Tracking of Extreme Weather Anomalies in Medium-Range Forecasts
department: National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)
description:
• Problem Statement Identifying and tracking the exact geographic footprints of extreme weather anomalies (such as severe cyclones, heat domes, or cold waves) within massive global Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) outputs is computationally intensive and heavily reliant on manual interpretation. In medium-range forecasting (3 to 10 days), atmospheric chaos renders traditional deterministic models highly uncertain.
Furthermore, standard deep learning models (like standard CNNs or U-Nets) suffer from spectral smoothing-they tend to 'average out' spatial data, which destroys the extreme amplitudes (the high-intensity peaks of rainfall or wind speed) that forecasters actually need to track. There is a critical gap between broad, coarse 12 km global ensemble datasets and localized, high-fidelity threat tracking.
• Proposed Solution We propose an automated, state-of-the-art AI tracking and downscaling pipeline that shifts the paradigm from manual weather data sorting to automated, physics-informed anomaly tracking.Instead of relying on a single deterministic forecast run, our system directly processes multivariable, 4D Ensemble Prediction Systems (EPS) data.The system uses a two-stage hybrid AI architecture to solve the spectral smoothing problem:First, it utilizes a graph neural network (GNN) to map atmospheric variables onto a spherical mesh,instantly isolating moving anomalies and calculating their trajectory over a 3- to 10-day forecast window.
Second, it pipes this isolated region into a generative diffusion model to perform statistical downscaling. This physics-constrained generative model mathematically derives a hyper-local 5km subgrid impact zone without flattening or blurring the severe amplitudes of the extreme weather event.
• Technical Methodology & Architecture Spherical Anomaly Tracking (Stage 1 GNN): To eliminate the geographic distortions caused by processing the spherical Earth on flat 2D pixel grids, the system maps the 12 km NCMRWF Global Ensemble (NEPS-G) grids directly onto an icosahedral mesh. The message-passing GNN calculates the Extreme Forecast Index (EFI) against a 30-year historical ERA5 baseline distribution to isolate standard deviations and draw a macro-scale temporal bounding box around the anomaly's trajectory.
Amplitude-Preserving Downscaling (Stage 2 Diffusion): The system passes the cropped, macroscale bounding box into a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model. Rather than optimizing for mean errors (which blurs peaks), the diffusion model learns the physical relationships between synoptic-scale features and regional topography. It iteratively generates high-resolution, high-amplitude local weather scenarios, downscaling the 12 km grid into a 5 km grid.
Physics-Informed Constraints: To ensure the model remains scientifically accurate, we embed fluid dynamics and thermodynamic conservation laws directly into the neural network's loss function. The model is mathematically penalized if it generates physically impossible weather states (e.g., severe downpours missing corresponding moisture convergence vectors).
• Datasets and Tools ? AI Frameworks: PyTorch / JAX (engineered with custom, physics-guided loss functions),Deep Graph Library (DGL) for icosahedral mesh networks, and Hugging Face Diffusers for generative downscaling.
? Data Wrangling & Geospatial Tools: Xarray and Dask for processing parallelized, multigigabyte 4D NetCDF/GRIB2 arrays; MetPy for physical meteorological equations;
Cartopy for geographical map projections.
? Training & Testing Datasets:
? Baseline: Historical IMDAA / ERA5 reanalysis data to establish the climatological norm.
? Forecast Inputs: Historical NCUM (12 km deterministic) and NEPS-G (12 km global ensemble) datasets containing documented extreme historical events (e.g., Cyclone Amphan, severe North India heatwaves).
• Expected Outcome & Key Deliverables The Tracking Core: A production-ready Spatio-Temporal GNN module that continuously processes global NWP streams to output dynamic, automated 4D bounding boxes around evolving weather threats.
The Downscaling Core: A generative diffusion module capable of ingesting a 12 km resolution anomaly slice and outputting a probabilistically sound, 5 km resolution sub-grid array that retains extreme value amplitudes.
The Visualization & Alert Dashboard: An automated system that translates the mathematical 5 km centroid arrays into clean, geographic visual layers.
The Alerting API: A lightweight, production-ready REST API that programmatically drops a pinpoint coordinate at the core of the severe anomaly and triggers categorized spatial alerts (low, moderate, and severe) across a precise 5 km geographical impact radius.
• Use Cases & Societal Impact Eliminating Alert Fatigue for the NDRF: Current weather alerts are often too broad, covering entire states or districts, which leads to public complacency. This solution allows meteorologists to issue hyper-localized, highly targeted warnings. It changes a generic'heavy rain in the district' alert into a precise 'high risk of flash flooding within your specific 5 km radius in the next 12 hours' alert, empowering first responders to deploy assets perfectly.
Protecting Rural Economies: Grants farming communities a highly accurate, 3- to 10- day lead time regarding localized catastrophic anomalies like sudden frost, hail, or heat domes. This structural foresight lets farmers alter harvesting schedules or apply cropprotection covers, shielding rural livelihoods from sudden climate shocks.
Democratizing Supercomputing Power: Once this hybrid AI pipeline is trained, it processes live inference data on a standard cloud GPU node in seconds, making high-fidelity climate forecasting highly affordable and easily accessible.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, deep learning, generative applied to a disaster management problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Disaster Management. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on api, model, architecture. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 25/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Driven Spatio-Temporal Tracking of Extreme Weather Anomalies in Medium-Range Forecasts

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an AI pipeline that automatically finds and tracks severe cyclones, heat domes, and cold waves inside massive global weather forecast datasets, without losing the extreme intensity peaks that standard AI models tend to blur away.
overview.why_it_matters: Forecasters currently do this tracking manually across enormous datasets. Automating it, while preserving the actual extreme values that matter most, directly speeds up and sharpens medium-range disaster preparedness.
pain_points: Manual interpretation of massive global NWP outputs for extreme weather tracking doesn't scale.
Standard deep learning models (CNNs, U-Nets) smooth out the extreme intensity peaks that matter most.
A gap exists between coarse global ensemble data and the localized, high-fidelity tracking forecasters actually need.
overview.background: Tracking extreme weather anomalies in medium-range (3-10 day) global forecast data is currently manual and computationally intensive, and standard deep learning approaches suffer from spectral smoothing that destroys the extreme values forecasters need to track.
overview.whats_being_asked: An automated AI tracking and downscaling pipeline processing multivariable 4D Ensemble Prediction System data, using a physics-informed, two-stage approach that avoids spectral smoothing to preserve extreme-value signals.
expected_solution: Automated anomaly detection and tracking from global 4D EPS data.
A method specifically avoiding spectral smoothing/averaging of extreme values.
Two-stage tracking and downscaling architecture from coarse to high-fidelity resolution.
Physics-informed model design rather than pure black-box learning.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. This explicitly names a known, real technical limitation (spectral smoothing in standard CNNs/U-Nets) and asks for a solution, genuinely advanced, research-adjacent meteorological deep learning.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Very high. Physics-informed deep learning avoiding spectral smoothing, processing 4D ensemble data, is genuinely advanced technical territory, likely the most technically demanding PS in this weather-forecasting cluster.

competitive_landscape.note: Extremely technical, research-grade meteorological AI PS, very few teams will have the specific expertise (physics-informed deep learning, spectral preservation techniques) to attempt this meaningfully.

innovation.note: Explicitly addresses a known, real limitation of standard deep learning for weather data, genuine advanced research territory.

invention.note: Physics-informed architecture avoiding spectral smoothing on 4D ensemble data is among the most technically demanding asks in this batch.

technical_feasibility.note: Full 4D EPS data processing at scale with genuine physics-informed spectral preservation is a research-grade challenge, well beyond typical 36-hour scope for a fully validated system.

impact_and_benefits.note: If genuinely achieved, has significant value for medium-range disaster preparedness, though achieving it fully is the hard part.

architecture.note: Multi-stage, physics-informed deep learning architecture is genuinely advanced, among the most architecturally sophisticated PS in this batch.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow. Extremely ambitious and technically demanding, a genuinely complete solution is closer to a research paper's worth of work than a 36-hour hackathon build. A strong submission should scope to demonstrating the core spectral-preservation concept on a smaller test case, being explicit about the gap to the PS's full ambition.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Explicitly and precisely names the real technical failure mode (spectral smoothing) it wants solved, giving a very specific, well-defined, and genuinely meaningful technical target.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: This is one of the most technically demanding PS in the entire dataset, attempting the full scope (4D EPS processing, two-stage physics-informed architecture, full validation) in 36 hours isn't realistic, scope aggressively.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope to demonstrating the core spectral-preservation concept, showing your architecture preserves extreme values better than a standard CNN/U-Net baseline on a smaller test case, rather than attempting the full-scale 4D EPS pipeline.

idea_0_4: Scope aggressively: focus on demonstrating spectral preservation (your model retains extreme values that a standard CNN/U-Net baseline would smooth away) on a smaller, manageable test case.
Source public NWP ensemble or reanalysis data for a known extreme weather event (a documented heatwave or cyclone) as your test case.
Split: one person on the baseline standard model (for comparison), one on your physics-informed/spectral-preserving approach.
prototype_4_22: Build a standard CNN/U-Net baseline model on your test data, this demonstrates the smoothing problem you're solving.

Build your alternative architecture specifically designed to preserve extreme values (techniques like specialized loss functions penalizing smoothing, or architecture choices avoiding aggressive downsampling).
Compare both models' outputs on the same extreme event test case.
integration_22_30: Quantify the difference, does your approach genuinely preserve extreme values better than the baseline, measure this directly, not just visually.
Test on your chosen historical extreme event, comparing both models against the documented real extreme values.
Refine your approach based on this comparison.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization directly comparing baseline (smoothed) versus your approach (extreme-value-preserving) output against real historical extreme values.
Rehearse explaining the spectral smoothing problem and your specific solution clearly, this is a technical concept that needs a clear explanation for non-specialist judges too.
Prepare to discuss what full-scale 4D EPS deployment would require beyond your scoped demonstration.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a direct, quantified comparison between a standard CNN/U-Net baseline (visibly smoothing out extreme values) and your approach (preserving them) on the same real historical extreme event, that head-to-head comparison is the clearest possible proof you solved the actual named problem.

strengths: Very specific, well-defined, genuinely meaningful technical target (spectral smoothing) to solve.
A scoped demonstration of the core concept is achievable even though the full PS ambition isn't.
weaknesses: One of the most technically demanding PS in the entire batch, full scope is not realistically achievable in 36 hours.
Requires genuinely advanced deep learning expertise, not broadly accessible to a general ML team.

roles_needed: Data engineering person (4D ensemble data handling)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS needs a genuinely strong, advanced deep learning practitioner, not a general ML team, be honest about your team's capability level before committing.
team_fit.approach: Build the baseline comparison model first, it's both useful evidence and ensures you have something working even if your advanced approach needs more tuning time.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard CNN/U-Net baseline model scaffolding, useful as your comparison point.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing a genuinely effective physics-informed, spectral-preserving architecture, that's advanced, research-level ML engineering requiring real expertise, not a default pattern.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: AI-generated architecture suggestions for this genuinely research-grade problem, without deep expert validation, risk producing something that looks sophisticated but doesn't actually solve the real spectral smoothing problem being tested for.

data_resource_availability.status: Public NWP ensemble/reanalysis data covering documented historical extreme weather events genuinely exists and is accessible.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable, though 4D ensemble data at full scale is large, plan for a scoped-down test case.

judge_qna.question: How do you actually know your approach preserves extreme values better than a standard model, not just visually but quantitatively?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your direct, quantified comparison, extreme-value preservation metrics (e.g. peak intensity retained) for your approach versus the baseline on the same real test case.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your approach's tradeoff, does preserving extremes cost you anything in overall accuracy or computational cost?

judge_qna.question: This is an extremely ambitious PS, what's the honest gap between what you built and the full described system?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct about your scoping choice, you demonstrated the core spectral-preservation concept on a focused test case rather than the full 4D EPS pipeline at scale, and describe what scaling up would require.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the single biggest technical hurdle between your demonstration and a full operational system?
